blocks.prompt: 6 (i) Find a vector whose magnitude is 5 and is parallel to \(3\underline{i} + 4\underline{j} - \underline{k}\).
blocks.explanation:
We need a vector with a given length (5) along a given direction.
Plan: make the unit vector of the given vector (length 1), then multiply it by 5.
Multiplying by \(-5\) instead gives the parallel vector in the opposite sense.
steps:
Given: direction \(3\underline{i} + 4\underline{j} - \underline{k}\), required length 5.
To find: a vector of length 5 parallel to it.
Method: required vector \(= 5 \times\) (unit vector in the given direction).

Length of the given vector
\[\sqrt{3^2 + 4^2 + (-1)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{9 + 16 + 1} = \sqrt{26}\]
Why: Magnitude formula.

Unit vector, then multiply by 5
\[\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{26}}(3\underline{i} + 4\underline{j} - \underline{k})\]
\[= \dfrac{15}{\sqrt{26}}\underline{i} + \dfrac{20}{\sqrt{26}}\underline{j}\]
\[\quad - \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{26}}\underline{k}\]
Why: Dividing by \(\sqrt{26}\) gives length 1; multiplying by 5 gives length 5 in the same direction.

Check the length
\[\dfrac{225 + 400 + 25}{26} = \dfrac{650}{26} = 25\]
\[\sqrt{25} = 5 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The length comes out exactly 5.

blocks.prompt: 6 (ii) Find a vector whose magnitude is 7 and is parallel to \(-\underline{i} + \underline{j} + \underline{k}\).
blocks.explanation:
We need a vector with a given length (7) along a given direction.
Plan: make the unit vector of the given vector (length 1), then multiply it by 7.
Multiplying by \(-7\) instead gives the parallel vector in the opposite sense.
steps:
Given: direction \(-\underline{i} + \underline{j} + \underline{k}\), required length 7.
To find: a vector of length 7 parallel to it.
Method: required vector \(= 7 \times\) (unit vector in the given direction).

Length of the given vector
\[\sqrt{(-1)^2 + 1^2 + 1^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{3}\]
Why: Magnitude formula.

Unit vector, then multiply by 7
\[\dfrac{7}{\sqrt{3}}(-\underline{i} + \underline{j} + \underline{k})\]
\[= -\dfrac{7}{\sqrt{3}}\underline{i} + \dfrac{7}{\sqrt{3}}\underline{j}\]
\[\quad + \dfrac{7}{\sqrt{3}}\underline{k}\]
Why: Dividing by \(\sqrt{3}\) gives length 1; multiplying by 7 gives length 7 in the same direction.

Check the length
\[3 \times \dfrac{49}{3} = 49\]
\[\sqrt{49} = 7 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The length comes out exactly 7.
